messages:
sara: 09:12 UTC - Seeing a sharp spike of 502/504s from hosted inference API across eu-west and us-east. Alerts show a surge in `backend_gateway` latencies and repeated `ERR_CACHE_CONN_TIMEOUT` entries when contacting prefix-cache (redis). Customers reporting timeouts on /v1/generate.

alex: oncall - grabbing logs now. Which service is throwing the 502s? Any correlation with recent deploys?

sara: support - no deploys in last hour. Pasting a trimmed log snippet: 
```
[09:11:58] upstream read timeout contacting prefix-cache (redis://10.3.5.12:6379) err=CONN_TIMEOUT
[vhost=api.redwood.com route=/v1/generate] 502 Gateway Error
```

mina: infra - checking redis-prod cluster. host redis-prod-01 has client connections at 1024/1024 and a steady increase in `wait_count`. Looks like connection pool saturation + a small number of keys with very long TTL/large payloads.

jen: runtime - our request flow does a synchronous prefix lookup before scheduling to the model pool. If the prefix cache blocks (connection wait), the request sits and upstream gateway times out -> 502. This matches symptoms.

sara: repro from a customer's postman script: fire 8 concurrent /v1/generate calls with same `prefix_id` -> 2 succeed, others return 502 after ~3s.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) enable cache fallback (short-circuit to memcached/local LRU) for affected routes via feature flag, 2) temporarily increase redis client pool size on gateway services, 3) throttle noisy prefixes. I'll flip the flag and scale pools.

alex: flipping `cache_fallback=true` for api-gateway svc now. :hammer_and_wrench:

deploy-bot: deploy started by alex (config change: cache_fallback=true) - rolling 3/3 instances in api-gateway.

jen: monitoring - after flag flip error rate dropped ~70% within 60s, latency still elevated for a subset of requests. Could be hotspot prefixes causing backend pressure. Recommend collecting prefix hit rates and sizes.

mina: infra - I increased `maxclients` on redis-prod (non-disruptive) and added an additional redis replica to the pool. Also opened a ticket to rotate the noisy node and check for long-running blocking commands.

alex: follow-up actions: 1) add metrics to capture per-prefix connection wait and payload size, 2) implement per-prefix concurrency limits and dedupe requests for the same prefix, 3) review TTLs and chunk large prefix blobs into smaller objects.

tim: product - need a short status update for customers. Sara, can you post to status.redwood.com and DM top affected accounts? We should offer mitigation steps (reduce concurrency, avoid very large prefix objects) until infra changes fully roll out.

sara: support - will update status page and send proactive outreach to enterprise customers. Draft message: "We experienced degraded API availability due to a prefix cache backend saturation; we've applied a fallback and are increasing cache capacity. No model data was lost."

jen: postmortem notes to track: root cause = connection pool exhaustion on prefix-cache (redis) driven by a small number of very large/noisy prefix keys; short-term fix = cache fallback + pool increases; long-term = per-prefix throttling, dedupe, KV sharding.

mina: I scheduled maintenance window for redis-prod to reclaim resources and perform a controlled restart during low-traffic window.

alex: will open an internal RFC for prefix-caching hardening and add alerts for `client_connections / maxclients > 0.8` and sustained `wait_count > 100` to catch early.

sara: thanks all — continuing customer comms and monitoring. Will follow up in this thread with status updates. :white_check_mark:
